story.soThat: validation code has strongly-typed structures for sessions, findings, and discrepancies
story.tasks:
- [ ] Task 1: Implement Session model (AC: #1) - [ ] Create `rustybt/validation/models.py` file - [ ] Import required types: dataclass, field, datetime, Path, Literal, Optional, Any - [ ] Define Session dataclass with 9 fields and type hints - [ ] Add field defaults: findings=field(default_factory=list) - [ ] Add docstring explaining session lifecycle and ID format - [ ] Add example docstring showing typical Session instantiation
- [ ] Task 2: Implement Finding model (AC: #2) - [ ] Define Finding dataclass with 10 fields and type hints - [ ] Use Literal["data", "signals", "orders", "broker", "portfolio"] for layer - [ ] Use Optional[Literal["BUG", "DESIGN"]] for classification - [ ] Set default values: classification=None, rationale=None, investigated_by=None, investigated_at=None, resolved=False, rustybt_value=None, backtrader_value=None - [ ] Add docstring explaining BUG vs DESIGN classification
- [ ] Task 3: Implement Discrepancy model (AC: #3) - [ ] Define Discrepancy dataclass with 9 fields and type hints - [ ] Use str for layer (not Literal - allows flexibility) - [ ] Use Optional[str] for asset (some events are portfolio-wide) - [ ] Add docstring explaining tolerance-based comparison
- [ ] Task 4: Add type safety and module docstring (AC: #4) - [ ] Add module-level docstring to models.py explaining purpose - [ ] Verify all imports from typing module - [ ] Use Python 3.12+ syntax (| for Union types) - [ ] Add `from __future__ import annotations` for forward references if needed
- [ ] Task 5: Export models from package (AC: #5) - [ ] Edit `rustybt/validation/__init__.py` - [ ] Add `from .models import Session, Finding, Discrepancy` - [ ] Add `__all__ = ["Session", "Finding", "Discrepancy"]` - [ ] Verify import works: `python -c "from rustybt.validation import Session, Finding, Discrepancy"`
- [ ] Task 6: Add unit tests for models - [ ] Create `tests/validation/test_models.py` - [ ] Test Session instantiation with all required fields - [ ] Test Finding with BUG and DESIGN classifications - [ ] Test Discrepancy creation with tolerance exceeded - [ ] Test default values are applied correctly - [ ] Test type hints are enforced (mypy check)

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
1. **Session model implemented** - `Session` dataclass captures validation session metadata - Fields: id (str), created_at (datetime), strategy_name (str), rustybt_version (str), backtrader_version (str), python_version (str), status (Literal), data_fixture (Path), findings (list[Finding]) - ID format: `{YYYYMMDD}-{HHMMSS}-{strategy_name}` - Status values: "IN_PROGRESS", "COMPLETED", "FAILED"
2. **Finding model implemented** - `Finding` dataclass captures layer discrepancies and classifications - Fields: id (str), layer (Literal), description (str), classification (Optional[Literal]), rationale (Optional[str]), investigated_by (Optional[str]), investigated_at (Optional[datetime]), resolved (bool), rustybt_value (Any), backtrader_value (Any) - Layer values: "data", "signals", "orders", "broker", "portfolio" - Classification values: "BUG", "DESIGN", None
3. **Discrepancy model implemented** - `Discrepancy` dataclass captures specific value mismatches during comparison - Fields: layer (str), event (str), timestamp (datetime), asset (Optional[str]), field (str), rustybt_value (Any), backtrader_value (Any), tolerance (Any), exceeded_by (Any)
4. **Models are type-safe** - All models use Python 3.12+ type hints and are mypy-strict compatible
5. **Models are exported** - Models are importable from `rustybt.validation`

doc.title: Architecture - Data Models
doc.snippet:
Session Model: - id: Unique session identifier - status: IN_PROGRESS, COMPLETED, FAILED - findings: List of discrepancies found
Finding Model: - classification: BUG (fix required) or DESIGN (intentional difference) - rationale: Explanation for DESIGN classification

constraint.description: Python 3.12+ Type Hints: Use `str | None` syntax, `list[T]` generics.
Mypy Strict: No implicit Any, fully typed signatures.

tests.standards: Unit tests for model instantiation and defaults. Type checking via mypy.

Test invalid enum values (though static analysis catches this).
